answer.text:
Priya Nair (Acme IT Integration Lead) raised the operator identifier field in the fresh feed at the Fresh Phase 2 go/no-go call on 17 November 2025, noting that the waste write-off records carry the operator and that per-employee waste figures should not leave their estate without a consultation, citing the works council. [1] [2] [3] [4] [5] [6]

Nadia Haddad (RELEX Solution Consultant) agreed to exclude the field at source and to confirm in writing the next day; the decision to drop it at the extract was voiced across the call, with the opening of that sentence spoken by an unidentified speaker and the completion by Nadia Haddad. [7] [8] [9] [10] [11]

On 18 November 2025 Priya Nair confirmed in writing that the exclusion was a condition rather than a request, and on 19 November 2025 Nadia Haddad confirmed that OP_ID would be dropped at the extract from the next run, which was Friday night. [12] [13]

The weekly update of 24 November 2025 recorded the OP_ID field exclusion as agreed and confirmed in writing. [14]

On the cutover call of 11 December 2025, Kwame Boateng stated the field was excluded at the extract from 21 November 2025 and confirmed in writing to Priya, and Priya Nair acknowledged receipt. [15] [16] [17]

On whether the field had already been sent anywhere: yes. On 24 November 2025 Kwame Boateng reported that OP_ID was present in the raw landing zone for every daily file since 14 February, though not carried into the aggregated waste tables, and that it was present in the row-level reconciliation extracts produced in June and September for the data quality review; two of those extracts were emailed as attachments, once to Priya and once to a distribution list of nine people including three at Meridian. He stated he could purge the landing zone but could not purge the attachments. [18]

citations.quote:
This email originated from outside of RELEX. Be careful of attachments and links from unknown senders. Report suspicious emails using the report button.

Nadia,

Following Monday's call, confirming this as a condition rather than a request.

The waste write-off extract currently includes OP_ID, a six digit operator identifier
identifying the individual who scanned the item out. Examples from the November file:

447102  Marika Lindqvist, store 118 Vantaa, nights
448933  Osman Yildirim, store 118 Vantaa
451207  Heidi Salminen, store 094 Espoo

This has been in every file since February. It must be excluded at source before the
next extract runs. Please confirm the field is dropped and tell me what you have done
with the files already delivered.

Our works council will ask. I would rather answer them than be asked.

If the answer to the second question is complicated, put it on the agenda for the
January session rather than replying to this.

Priya Nair
IT Integration Lead

Checked the 17 November 2025 go/no-go transcript: Priya Nair raised the field (utterances 100-104, 147, 149); the drop-at-extract sentence spans an unknown speaker (150) and Nadia Haddad (151, 153, 154); Nadia's written-confirmation promise is utterance 139.

Checked the email thread: Priya's condition email is 18 November (E07M004); Nadia's confirmation with Friday-night next run is 19 November (E07M003); Kwame's historic-files answer is 24 November (E07M002).
Verified numbers against cited passages: 14 February, June, September, nine people, three at Meridian, two emailed attachments (E07M002); 21 November (T18U0068); Friday night next run (E07M003).
Corrected attribution: the draft attributed the entire drop-at-extract statement to Nadia; utterance 150 is an unknown speaker, with Nadia completing it (151, 153, 154).

Corrected the cutover-call citation: the 21 November effective date was stated by Kwame Boateng (utterance 68), not a range starting at 67 alone; utterance 67 (Ana Duarte) names the field and utterance 69 (Priya) acknowledges receipt.
